record.original_question: (a) Does there exist a finitely generated simple group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth? (b) Does there exist a finitely generated hereditarily just-infinite group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth?

evidence.quote: (a) Does there exist a finitely generated simple group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth? (b) Does there exist a finitely generated hereditarily just-infinite group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group with a finite generating set $S$ (assumed symmetric, $S=S^{-1}$). Let $B_S(n)=\{g\in G:\ell_S(g)\le n\}$ where $\ell_S$ is the word length, and define the exponential growth rate
$$\omega(G,S)=\lim_{n\to\infty}|B_S(n)|^{1/n}\in[1,\infty).$$
$G$ is said to be of exponential growth if $\omega(G,S)>1$ for some (equivalently every) finite generating set $S$, and of uniformly exponential growth if
$$\omega(G):=\inf_S \omega(G,S)>1,$$
where the infimum is taken over all finite generating sets $S$ of $G$.

Recall that $G$ is simple if it has no proper nontrivial normal subgroup, and $G$ is just-infinite if it is infinite and every proper quotient is finite. $G$ is hereditarily just-infinite if it is residually finite and every finite-index subgroup of $G$ is just-infinite.

Decide each of the following:
(a) Does there exist a finitely generated simple group of exponential growth that is not of uniformly exponential growth?
(b) Does there exist a finitely generated hereditarily just-infinite group of exponential growth that is not of uniformly exponential growth?

The questions are recorded as new problems in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook update, and related work on uniform exponential growth (e.g. for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces) does not address simple or hereditarily just-infinite groups specifically. The general problem of constructing groups of exponential but non-uniformly exponential growth (Wilson's examples) remains active, but no such construction is known to be simple or hereditarily just-infinite.
